question: Does a contract's own monthly trading (volume, open interest, price, funding) rank it as likely to stop trading within 3 months, better than the rule that flags the lowest-volume contracts?

excluded.crypto_kept: CFGUSDT life 1, GRVTUSDT life 1, LITUSDT life 2, MOONSHOTUSDT life 1, PREDICTUSDT life 1

verdict: **On the fair test (final full month dropped), the frozen full-feature logistic model is ahead but not decisively.** The baseline is the lowest-volume-rank rule (b), and the headline metric is precision among the top 5% of live contracts each month on the 2026 lock-box (3,730 contract-months over 7 origin months, 61 delisted contracts, base rate 3.9%). With the final full month before the last trading day kept, the logistic model beats the baseline: 0.270 against 0.151, paired difference +0.119 [+0.097, +0.145]. With that month dropped, since it often holds the delisting announcement, it is ahead but not decisively: 0.174 against 0.125, paired difference +0.049 [-0.016, +0.081] (PR-AUC difference +0.041 [+0.002, +0.092]); 59% of the main-run gain, more than half, disappears when that month is dropped. In cross-validation (36 test months, 2023-01 to 2025-12) the same model is ahead but not decisively with the month kept (+0.018 [-0.008, +0.042]) and is ahead but not decisively without it (+0.007 [-0.019, +0.022]). LightGBM on the same features does not beat the baseline on the fair lock-box test (+0.000 [-0.005, +0.022]), and the falling-volume rule (a) stays near chance (0.038 against a base rate of 0.025). So a contract's own monthly trading does flag likely delistings, mostly through its volume rank (rule (b) alone reaches 5.0 times the base rate on the fair lock-box test) and its open-interest rank (open interest is 40% of the tree model's attributions); the extra features add an edge with the same sign in CV and the lock-box, but its size is not established once the announcement month is removed.
